question.text: Which statement about the LLP structure for AIFs in India is CORRECT?

answer.text: LLPs are regulated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and investor details become public
LLPs offer better tax efficiency than trusts for AIFs
LLPs can have unlimited partners without compliance

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.103) notes that LLPs are regulated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), and that investor details come under the public domain through MCA filings. It also states that, in an LLP-structured AIF, all investors become partners and that partner entry and exit is cumbersome, with higher overall compliance. The Trap: Investor details in an LLP are not "completely private" — MCA filings make them publicly accessible. The workbook does not say LLPs are more tax-efficient than trusts for AIFs, nor that they can have unlimited partners without compliance. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook p.103 (LLP — MCA regulation; investor details in the public domain; partners' entry/exit cumbersome; higher compliance).
